Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:11: And besides being called a scoffer, one who speaks idle words also transgresses a positive commandment, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:7), "and you shall speak of them" - and so in Tractate Yoma, first chapter (19b), in these words: our Rabbis taught, "and you shall speak of them" - and not in prayer. "Of them" you have permission to speak, and not of other matters. "And you shall speak of them" - make them fixed. Rava said, whoever engages in idle conversation transgresses a positive commandment, as it is said, "and you shall speak of them," and not of other matters. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said, he transgresses a negative commandment, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:8), "all things are wearisome, man cannot speak [of them all]" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:12: And especially students of Torah must be very careful of idle words, for they said in the Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah (1:21), on the verse (1:3), "for the fragrance of your good oils" - in these words: what is oil like? A full cup does not overflow with other liquids [as easily], so words of Torah do not overflow with words of mockery. Just as with this oil, if a cup full of oil is in your hand and a drop of water falls into it, a drop of oil comes out to match it - so if a word of Torah enters the heart, a word of mockery comes out to match it; if a word of mockery enters the heart, a word of Torah comes out to match it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:13: And included in this group is the group who play dice and other kinds of games - even if they do not play to win money from each other, which would involve theft, there is still the matter of "two who sit together without words of Torah between them, this is a session of scoffers," as explained. And this resembles the kinds of games mentioned in Tractate Avodah Zarah (18b), where they said that they are a session of scoffers, in these words: our Rabbis taught, whoever goes to the stadiums or the circuses and sees there the snake-charmers, the buffoons, the masked performers, the tumblers, the acrobats, the [various entertainers] - this is a session of scoffers, and concerning them Scripture says (Psalms 1:1), "who has not walked," and so on, "but whose desire is in the Torah of the LORD" - from this you learn that these things bring a person to the nullification of Torah - to this point. And Rashi explains "bukyon," and so on, as kinds of mockery - from this you learn, from its being juxtaposed with "but... in the Torah," that whoever goes to these does not desire the Torah of the LORD - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that since he is idle from the Torah of the LORD in these kinds of games, they are called a session of scoffers - and the same applies to other kinds of games.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:14: And there are those who have permitted themselves games of dice, saying that it is something that sharpens the mind - and I saw fit to expose their error, so that they not become clever with arguments of their own inclination against the Torah of the LORD. First, what Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in Sefer HaYirah, that one who speaks idle words is like one who denies the fundamental principle, for he does not believe that the whole earth is full of His glory - for one who believes that he stands before the blessed and exalted King would not do anything against His will. And in my eyes this matter is more difficult than all other transgressions - for with all other transgressions, if the sinner sins momentarily, suddenly led astray by his inclination and not placing the fear of the LORD before him, his punishment is not so great; but this one, who with contempt of soul sits an hour or three hours, and sometimes the whole day, does not remember the LORD before him, and does not say in his heart, before whom do I stand and play, stand and provoke - and is not ashamed before His greatness and does not fear His judgment, and transgresses the negative commandment "take heed to yourself, lest you forget the LORD your God" - he forgets the LORD, and even so sits and plays - behold, he willfully disgraces the LORD and His Torah, saying in his heart that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not punish the group of scoffers - and he denies the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and is a Sadducee. He resembles those about whom the Holy One, blessed be He, complained to the prophet Ezekiel, who worshipped idols in secret and said (Ezekiel 8:12), "the LORD has forsaken the land, the LORD does not see us" - and these worship idols openly, meaning they give an excuse as though it were permitted to do so publicly, with no one protesting against them. And if our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Nedarim 22b) of one who becomes angry, that the Shechinah is not significant in his eyes, all the more so should this be said of this group, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:15: And further, we find in the Talmud (Niddah 13a) concerning one who holds his member while urinating, that they said to Rabbi Eliezer that he appeared to have a crushed member and thus cast an aspersion on his children, that they were illegitimate - and he answered, better that he cast an aspersion on his children, that they are illegitimate, than that he make himself a wicked man before the Omnipresent for even one moment. And along these lines, all the more so, one who plays dice, making himself wicked before the Omnipresent for more than two hours, and possibly the whole day - this argument is one of reason.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:16: And further, in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, they said in Tractate Bava Batra (79a): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, whoever separates himself from words of Torah and occupies himself with idle conversation, fire consumes him, as it is said (Ezekiel 15:7), "and I will set My face against them; they shall go out from the fire, but the fire shall consume them." Further there, when Ravin came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan, whoever weakens himself from the words of Torah falls into Gehinnom, as it is said (Proverbs 21:16), "a man who strays from the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of the departed [refa'im]" - and "refa'im" refers only to those who descend to Gehinnom, as it is said (ibid. 9:18), "but he does not know that the departed are there, in the depths of Sheol," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:17: And Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, peace be upon him, wrote in Sefer Menorat HaMaor (letter 31), in these words: and one who occupies himself with idle matters, even if there is no forbidden speech in it, loses the time he could have occupied with words of Torah to acquire the life of the World to Come - and it appears from his mind that he disdains the words of the Name and the reward of the World to Come, as we read in the chapter "Chelek" (99a): it was taught, Rabbi Meir says, whoever learns Torah and does not teach it, this is "for he has despised the word of the LORD"; Rabbi Nehorai says, whoever could occupy himself with Torah and does not - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:18: And not only that, but even one who could occupy himself with Torah and does not wish to, even if he does not speak words of mockery, his session is called a session of scoffers, as we learned in chapter 3 of Avot, "two who sit together without words of Torah between them, this is a session of scoffers," and so on. And it is not enough that he sins against his own soul and loses the life of the World to Come and inherits Gehinnom, but he also causes the multitude to sin - for by occupying himself with idle conversation he draws the heart of the multitude to be idle with him, and their sin depends on him, as we learned in chapter 5 of Avot, "Jeroboam sinned and caused the multitude to sin, the sin of the multitude is dependent on him," as it is said (2 Kings 13:2), "because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and caused Israel to sin." And they also punish him by not giving him the means to repent, than which there is no greater punishment, as we read in the chapter "Yom HaKippurim" (Yoma 87a): whoever gives merit to the multitude, no sin comes through him; and whoever causes the multitude to sin is not given the means to repent - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:19: And let not the speaker say, who can be careful to keep all the words of our Rabbis, so I shall be careful now about this one - and since he is not careful about the others, he shall not be careful about this one either. This argument too is rejected, for one transgression drags another (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 2), and if he is not careful about this one, his inclination will bring him to sin in all four groups that do not see the countenance of the Shechinah, in a manner that he shall be excluded from the World to Come - and woe to him who says with his mouth that he does not wish to see the countenance of the Shechinah, in order to fulfill the will of his inclination and be among the group of scoffers and the other groups. But if he sanctifies himself in this one, "whoever comes to be purified is assisted" (Yoma 38b), and he shall not sin in the other groups and shall be saved from them, as they said, of blessed memory (Yoma 39a), "a person who sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him much."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:20: And those who play dice and other kinds of games on festivals and appointed times, woe to their souls, for they have done themselves harm - for the days of the appointed times are days of judgment, as they said, of blessed memory (Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, mishnah 1), "at four points the world is judged: on Passover, concerning the grain; on Shavuot [Atzeret], concerning the fruit of the tree; on Rosh Hashanah, all who come into the world pass before Him like a flock; on Sukkot, they are judged concerning water." Behold, all the appointed times are days of judgment, and therefore they said (Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, chapter 15, halachah 3) that Sabbaths and festivals were given to Israel only so that they occupy themselves with Torah. And they said (Kiddushin 40b), "a person should always view himself and the world as half meritorious and half guilty; if he does one meritorious deed, happy is he, for he has tipped himself and the whole world to the scale of merit, and if not, Heaven forfend, he has tipped it to the scale of guilt." It follows that a sinner then, in play and levity, is more severe than at other times of the year - for since the world is in judgment, through one sin the world might be tipped to the scale of guilt, and then all those poor who die or suffer from the poverty of hunger and thirst are all dependent on him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:21: And on the days of the appointed times, besides a person's sustenance depending on it, a person's life and soul also depend on judgment, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in his explanation of this Mishnah that we copied (Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, page 226b), that it all speaks of the souls being judged - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:22: And therefore it is fitting to distance oneself from all kinds of games, whether on weekdays or on the days of the appointed times, for the world and man are always in judgment, as we copied the teachings of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Parashat Vayechi, pages 226b-227a), and the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Rosh Hashanah 16a), in the Gate of Fear, chapter 11. And this sin causes sufferings and destruction to the world, according to the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 18b) - therefore one must be careful not to stumble further, and his repentance shall be accepted, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:23: And it appears that all those explanations stated there (Sanhedrin 99a), explaining the verse "for he has despised the word of the LORD," are all included in mockery, for the mocker is the one who disdains matters, as we have said. It says there: "for he has despised the word of the LORD" (Numbers 15:31) - this is one who says the Torah is not from Heaven. Another interpretation: this is a heretic. "And has broken His commandment" - this is one who breaks the covenant of the flesh. It was taught in another [teaching]: "for he has despised the word of the LORD" - this is one who says the Torah is not from Heaven; and even if he said the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this verse, that not the Holy One, blessed be He, but Moses said it of his own accord - this is "for he has despised the word of the LORD"; and even if he said the whole Torah is from Heaven except for this fine point, this a fortiori argument, this verbal analogy - this is "for he has despised the word of the LORD." It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say, whoever learns Torah and does not teach it, this is "for he has despised the word of the LORD." Rabbi Natan says, whoever does not pay attention to the Mishnah. Rabbi Nechemiah says, and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:24: And just as we are obligated to believe in the whole Torah of Moses, so we are obligated to believe in all the words of the Scribes, and what they said in Midrashim and Aggadot - and although it may appear to be something contrary to nature, we must attribute the deficiency to the limitation of our own understanding, and not to their teaching. And whoever mocks anything of their words is punished, as we say in the chapter "Osin Pasin" (Eruvin 21b): Rav Papa said in the name of Rabbah bar Ulla, whoever mocks the words of the Sages is judged with boiling excrement - and so they said in Gittin (57a) - and so we find that that student was punished for mocking Rabbi Yochanan's words, when he said that the Holy One, blessed be He, would in the future bring precious stones thirty by thirty cubits, and so on, as it appears in Bava Batra (75a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:25: Concerning the punishment of the group of flatterers, they said, of blessed memory, in the chapter "Arvei Pesachim" (113b), that there are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates: one who speaks one thing with his mouth and another with his heart - this is the trait of flattery; one who knows testimony for his fellow and does not testify for him; and one who sees nakedness in his fellow and testifies against him alone.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:26: We read in Sanhedrin (52a): Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, what is the meaning of what is written (Psalms 35:16), "with flattering mockers of feasts, they gnashed their teeth at me"? Because of the flattery with which his congregation flattered Korach concerning matters of food, the prince of Gehinnom gnashed his teeth at them. In the chapter "Elu Ne'emarin" (Sotah 41b): Rabbi Elazar said, any person who has flattery in him falls into Gehinnom, as it is said (Isaiah 5:20), "woe to those who call evil good," and so on, and it is written right after it (ibid. 5:24), "therefore, as the tongue of fire devours stubble, and the flame consumes the chaff, their root shall be like rot, and their blossom shall go up like dust," and so on. And Rabbi Elazar said, whoever flatters his fellow will eventually fall into his hand, or into the hand of his son, or into the hand of his grandson - from where do we know this? From Chananiah ben Azzur, the false prophet, who was leading Israel astray, and Jeremiah the prophet said (Jeremiah 28:6), "thus may the LORD do; may the LORD confirm your words" - and because he did not protest but said "may the LORD confirm your words," he fell into the hand of his grandson, as it is said (Jeremiah 37:13), "and when he was at the gate of Benjamin, there was an officer of the guard there, whose name was Yiriyah, son of Shelemiah, son of Chananiah," and so on - "and the princes were angry with Jeremiah, and put him in the prison house." And any congregation that has flattery in it is as despicable as a menstruating woman, as it is said (Job 15:34), "for the congregation of the flatterer shall be desolate [galmud]" - and in the coastal cities they call a menstruating woman "galmuda."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:27: And in the Midrash they said: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta said, from the day the fist of flattery grew strong, judgments were perverted and deeds became corrupted, and no person could say to his fellow, my deeds are greater than yours. And even Jehoshaphat was fit to be judged, because he flattered Ahab - and where did he flatter him? As it is said (1 Kings 22:8), "and the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, there is still one more man to inquire of the LORD through him, but I hate him," and so on, "and Jehoshaphat said, let not the king say so" - and because he did not attack him but only said to him "let not the king say so," the prophet said to him (2 Chronicles 19:2), "should you help the wicked," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:28: And in Midrash Mishlei (chapter 26), on the verse (Proverbs 26:8), "like one who binds a stone in a sling, so is one who gives honor to a fool" - Rabbi Alexandri said, whoever gives honor to a fool is like one who throws a stone at Mercury [an idol] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:29: And this evil quality is more despicable in a Torah scholar than in the rest of the people, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:11), "for both prophet and priest have become flatterers [chanfu]," and so on. And they said in Tractate Yoma (72b): Rabbah said, any Torah scholar whose inside is not like his outside is not called a scholar, as it is said (Exodus 25:11), "within and without you shall overlay it [with gold]." Abaye said, he is called an abomination, as it is said (Job 15:16), "how much more one who is abominable and corrupt," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:30: And they said in Chagigah and Sotah (41b) that the enemies of Israel [euphemism for Israel] were obligated in destruction because they flattered King Agrippa, even though he was a king, humble and God-fearing - all the more so one who flatters the wicked. Rabbi Elazar said, any person who has flattery in him brings wrath to the world, as it is said, "and the flatterers of heart bring wrath" - and not only that, but his prayer is despised, as it is said (Job 36:13), "they do not cry out when He binds them" - Rashi, of blessed memory, explains, when sufferings come upon them, crying out shall not help them - and it is written (Job 27:8), "for what is the hope of the flatterer, though he gains," and so on, and it is written, "will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?" Further they said there: Rabbi Elazar said, any person who has flattery in him, even the fetuses in their mothers' wombs curse him, as it is said (Proverbs 24:24), "he who says to the wicked, you are righteous, peoples shall curse him [yikvuhu], nations shall abhor him" - and "yikvuhu" refers only to a curse, as it is said (Numbers 23:8), "how shall I curse [ekov] whom God has not cursed [kabo]" - and "le'umim" [nations] refers only to fetuses, as it is said (Genesis 25:23), "and the one people [le'om] shall be stronger than the other people [le'om]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:31: Further, they said in Midrash Mishlei (12:21): "no harm shall befall the righteous," when he walks in his integrity, "but the wicked are full of evil" - this refers to one who speaks one thing with his mouth and another with his heart, and the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him an abomination, as it is said, "lying lips are an abomination to the LORD." "But those who act faithfully are His delight" - this is one who conducts his business dealings faithfully - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:32: And because of the sin of flattery, people fall into the hand of their enemies and their spoil is plundered, as it is said (Isaiah 10:5), "woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger," and so on (10:6), "I will send him against a flattering [chanef] nation," and so on. And because of the sin of flattery, the Holy One, blessed be He, pours out His wrath on the land, and His hand is stretched out over the young men and over orphans and widows, as it is said (Isaiah 9:16), "therefore the LORD shall not rejoice over their young men," and so on, "for everyone is a flatterer [chanef] and an evildoer," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:33: Flattery is severe, for it is equal to idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed. Idolatry - from where? As it is written (Isaiah 32:6), "to practice flattery [chonef], to speak error [to'ah] against the LORD" - and "to'ah" refers only to idolatry, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:15), "they are vanity, a work of delusions [ta'tu'im]." Forbidden relations - from where? As it is said (Jeremiah 3:1), "behold, if a man sends away his wife," and so on, "would not the land be greatly flattered [chanof techenaf]?" Bloodshed - from where? As it is written (Psalms 106:38), "and the land was flattered [tech'naf] with blood."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:34: And because of the sin of flattery, the rains are withheld, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:2), "and you have flattered the land with your harlotries," and so on, and it is written right after, "and the showers were withheld," and so on. And because of the flattery a person practices in this world, he is judged in Gehinnom forever, for all eternity, as it is said (Isaiah 33:14), "the sinners in Zion are afraid, trembling has seized the flatterers [chanefim]; who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:35: And in Sotah (41b): Rabbi Yehudah bar Ma'aravaya, and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said, it is permitted to flatter the wicked in this world, as it is said (Isaiah 32:5), "the fool shall no longer be called noble, nor the miser said to be generous" - implying that in this world it is permitted. Reish Lakish said, from here (Genesis 33:10), "for I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you have received me favorably" - and this disagrees with Rabbi Levi, who said, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:36: Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, author of Sefer Menorat HaMaor, of blessed memory, wrote (letter 45), in these words: none of this speaks of praising evil qualities one practices, for concerning that they have already said that there are several sins involved. But what it says, "it is permitted to flatter," is this: although it is forbidden to honor the wicked, since they are haters of the Name, as it is written (Psalms 15:4), "in whose eyes a vile person is despised" - meaning that it is fitting for one who dwells in the tent of the LORD and abides on His holy mountain to despise the one who is despised in the eyes of the LORD, namely the wicked, and to honor those who fear the LORD, but not the wicked - and concerning this the sage said that the wicked, whose hand is strong and whose time is favorable, it is permitted to honor them out of fear, as one would honor men of force, but not out of love for them. And so they said in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 36), concerning the matter of Jacob who flattered Esau - from here they said, one may flatter the wicked in this world for the sake of peace, and your mnemonic is "Ahavah" [love], the initials of "flattering the wicked in this world" - and the intent is [that it be done] out of love, so that he may live to fulfill the commandments of his Creator. But whoever has the ability to protest and does protest, and takes his vengeance against the wicked in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, makes a covenant with him and with his seed after him, as He did for Pinchas.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:37: Further, concerning the punishment of the flatterer, they said, of blessed memory (Avot DeRabbi Natan 29:4), whoever flatters his fellow for the sake of honor will eventually be parted from him easily. And similar to this, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Sincerity of Deed, chapter 5), concerning one of the arguments of the inclination, that the inclination says one should do things that people will know of, so that a reputation for piety go out for him, until they learn from his deeds. And he answered that one should say to it, perhaps when I direct this in my deeds, the will intended by them will not be achieved through them, and it will occur to people that I am a flatterer in my deeds, and my deeds shall be in vain, in my intent for them being other than God. And it is said of a certain king, why did the reading of so-and-so not please you, though his voice was pleasant and skilled in the cantillation? He said to them, how should his reading please me? He does not read it except so that his reading please me and he find favor in my eyes because of it - but had this intent been for the will of the Creator alone, it would have pleased me. And so it may be said of anyone among those who pray in public, and the masters of the vision [prayer leaders] with new liturgical poems, who intends by his prayer to find favor in the eyes of people rather than the blessed God - it is not accepted by the Creator - to this point. It follows that included in the group of flatterers is one who performs a commandment for the blessed God with his intent being that people honor him for it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:38: And he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Sincerity of Deed, chapter 4), that one who performs a deed for the honor of people or out of fear of them does not serve the Creator but people, and is found not to recognize the Creator - and so is the matter of the idol-worshipper, that he worships the idols only because of his foolishness, not having recognized the Creator - and he wrote, in these words: and the idol-worshipper has an advantage over the flatterer in four things. The first, that the idol-worshipper nowadays is not warned by a prophet who would clarify to him the corruption of his thought with signs and wonders, but the flatterer within Torah has claims against him, in what he received of the commandments in the service of God and the warning against serving another. The second, that the idol-worshipper worships one who does not rebel against God, but the flatterer worships one who rebels against God, and also one who does not rebel against Him. The third, that the idol-worshipper worships one thing, while the flatterer has no limit to those he worships. The fourth, that the idol-worshipper's matter is not hidden from people, and they guard themselves from him because of the publicity of his denial of God, but the flatterer's denial is not apparent, and people trust him, and it is possible for him to harm them in a way not possible for another - and he is the greatest of the world's diseases, and is called in our language a flatterer, arrogant, and enticer - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:39: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash (Yalkut Mishlei, siman 961): Rabbi Chiya taught, they publicize the flatterers because of the desecration of the Name, as it is said (Proverbs 26:26), "his wickedness shall be revealed before the assembly," and it says (Ezekiel 3:20), "and when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, I will put a stumbling block before him" - and why did the Holy One, blessed be He, give them evil? In order to publicize their deeds to the creatures, so that nothing happen to him because of transgressions and they cry out against the attribute of judgment - go and learn from Doeg, who was head of the Sanhedrin, as it is said (1 Samuel 21:8), "the chief of Saul's shepherds" - and because he had the trait of slander, Scripture publicized it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:40: And in Sefer Menorat HaMaor of Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, he wrote, in these words: the flatterer is more despicable than the thief - for the thief steals money, but the flatterer steals people's minds. And the flatterers divide into three groups. The first group are those who flatter people so as to find favor in their eyes, and do not rebuke them for their evil deeds, but say, you are acting rightly - even though they are doing evil and improper deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:41: The second group is more despicable than the first - these are those who flatter the powerful and the wealthy, and subjugate their souls to them. To the powerful, so that they be made head over the community, and so that they inherit authority, and they strive to be honored through flattering them. To the wealthy, so that they plunder their money, and in order to benefit from it - and they remove their trust from the Holy One, blessed be He, and place their hope and expectation in people, supposing that their wealth will never end and never be lost from their hand - and in this they err, and concerning them it is said (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:42: The third group is more despicable still - these are those who flatter in religion, showing themselves to be righteous and diligent in synagogues, but their intent is to rise to greatness so that they be appointed leaders over the community, and to remove themselves from taxation, showing piety on their faces while their hearts are full of deceit and trickery - to this point. Some of his words and some of the essence of his wording I have not written, because of length.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:43: Further, Rabbeinu Yonah elaborated in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 3, letter 187) concerning the matter of the flatterers, and wrote nine divisions of them, and whoever wishes to see may find his book available. And the sum of his words is that one should not flatter the wicked or speak in his praise, whether to his face or not to his face, as it is said (Proverbs 28:4), "those who forsake the Torah praise the wicked." And along these lines it is possible to speak of one who appoints someone leader or scholar over the community when that person is unfit, and the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts punishment from the one who appointed him, for that scholar is found to destroy the world with his rulings, wrongly, and the like. And included in flattery is: if one does not wish to rebuke the people of his city, thinking they will not accept it from him, he is called a flatterer - so he wrote.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:44: I found written in a book that speaks of matters of piety, in these words: there are three whom one may flatter - his wife, for the sake of peace in the home; a creditor, so that he not oppress him; his teacher, so that he teach him Torah and commandments. And it is a great commandment to flatter one's students and colleagues so that they learn, and so that they heed his words to accept rebuke and fulfill commandments - and likewise for anyone he thinks he can draw to himself so that they heed him to fulfill the commandments - and if he comes to him angrily, they will not heed him, but through flattery they will accept his rebuke - and behold, it is a great commandment to flatter him, to bring out the precious from the vile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:45: And there is a person who accepts rebuke and reproof only calmly, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:17), "the words of the wise, spoken calmly, are heard." And there is one who needs a rebuke, as it is said (Proverbs 17:10), "a rebuke enters more deeply into a man of understanding [than a hundred blows into a fool]." And there is one for whom even striking will not help, as it is said, "than striking a fool a hundred times." If so, what shall be done? There is no remedy for him, but to expel him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:46: And there is a very evil kind of flattery, such as a person who speaks with his fellow and flatters him with sweet words, in order to draw him near and have him tell what is in his heart, and after he has trusted him and relies on him, he deals with him deceitfully - and this is as it is said (Proverbs 1:17), "for in vain is the net spread in the eyes of any bird" - (ibid. 1:18) "and they lie in wait for their own blood, they lurk secretly for their own souls" - for hunters scatter wheat in a net so that the birds come to eat, and then they are trapped - and this flatterer resembles this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:47: And the Sages forbade flattery, and said (Chullin 94a) that a person should not send a gift knowing that the recipient will not accept it, or press his fellow to eat with him knowing that he will not eat; and likewise, if a person wishes to open a barrel of wine to sell, and his fellow comes to buy wine, he should not say to him, I wish to open a barrel for your sake. And all this and the like is called "stealing minds," to flatter and steal people's minds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:48: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta said, from the day the fist of flattery grew strong, judgments were perverted and deeds became corrupted, and no person could say to his fellow, my deeds are greater than yours. Rabbi Elazar said, any person who has flattery brings wrath to the world, as it is said (Job 36:13), "and the flatterers of heart bring wrath" - and his prayer is not heard - even the fetuses in their mothers' wombs curse him in Gehinnom. And whoever flatters the wicked will eventually fall into his hand, and if he does not fall into his hand, he falls into the hand of his son or the hand of his grandson. And any woman who has flattery in her is as despicable as a menstruating woman, and in the end she is exiled (Sotah 42a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:49: Therefore a person shall distance himself from flattery, and shall not flatter a person to strengthen him in his wickedness - even if he stands to receive benefits from him, he should not flatter him - and he should not flatter his relatives or his children when they do not walk in a good path, for how many people remain in their wickedness because they see that they feel no shame for their ugly ways, and because they see that people flatter them. And there is nothing in the world that closes the gates of repentance like flattery.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:50: And there was a story of a certain worthy man who had a daughter to marry off, and there were in his city two young men, each of whom desired to take his daughter - and that worthy man went to judge between them, in order to test them, and he arranged for a certain man to pick a quarrel with him, so that afterward they would be brought to judge between the litigant and himself, in order to test them, and so they did. And of these two, one flattered that worthy man in order to marry his daughter, and would justify him in all his ways - and then he went and gave his daughter to the one who had found him liable, [saying] "for he is a good man," so said the worthy man, "because he did not flatter me and did not show me favoritism" (Sefer Chasidim, siman 942).
